Bug 1833237 - Vendor libwebrtc from f0be3bee1f

(skip-generation)

Upstream commit: https://webrtc.googlesource.com/src/+/f0be3bee1fc17d96354ce3c9bf457673b82e7d2d
    Add pipewire/portal video capture support

    This makes it possible to access cameras through xdg-desktop-portal and
    pipewire.

    For pipewire, a shared state is needed between the enumeration and the
    creation of camera object. So a new API is needed with a shared options
    object that holds the state and can be used to choose which backend to try.

fix_commit.message: Bug 1942551 - WebRTC backport: PipeWire camera: Fix cleanup order r=pehrsons,webrtc-reviewers
fix_commit.author: Jan Grulich

findings.title: Use-After-Free due to incorrect cleanup order in PipeWireNode destructor
findings.message: The destructor calls pw_proxy_destroy() before spa_hook_remove(), which destroys the proxy object before removing the hook that is associated with it. The hook contains a listener_list reference (proxy->listener_list) that is freed when pw_proxy_destroy() is called. The subsequent spa_hook_remove() then attempts to access this freed memory to remove the hook from the list, causing a use-after-free vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Swap the order of cleanup operations: remove the hook first before destroying the proxy object, since the hook is associated with the proxy and its listener_list.

ground_truth.root_cause: Incorrect destruction order in resource cleanup. The hook is associated with the proxy object and internally references the proxy's listener_list. By destroying the proxy first, the listener_list is freed, but the hook still holds a dangling reference to it. When spa_hook_remove() tries to remove the hook from the list, it accesses freed memory.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable cleanup sequence where pw_proxy_destroy() is called before spa_hook_remove(). The proxy destruction frees the listener_list that the hook still references, causing use-after-free when spa_hook_remove() tries to access it.

Constructor establishes the data dependency between proxy_ and node_listener_. Line 99-100 creates the proxy via pw_registry_bind, and line 108-109 registers the hook listener on that proxy using pw_node_add_listener. This shows the hook is tied to the proxy's lifetime and requires the proxy to remain valid during hook removal.

Triggers destruction of PipeWireNode objects via std::erase_if on nodes_ vector. When a unique_ptr<PipeWireNode, PipeWireNodeDeleter> is erased, it invokes the custom deleter containing the vulnerable cleanup sequence. This is a key path that exercises the bug during device removal.
